steps.message:
# Record yesterday's shipments

Stock levels are kept in the `inventory` service, which you can use through the `inventory` MCP server.

The warehouse system exported the orders shipped on 2026-09-13 to `/app/shipments/2026-09-13.jsonl`, one order per line: the order id, the warehouse it shipped from, and its lines (sku and quantity). Staff recorded some of these shipments by hand during the day, not always correctly. Make the stock records match the export:

- A shipped line is recorded by `adjust_stock` adjustments with reason `shipment`, the order id as reference, and the order's warehouse. For every line, the adjustments for that order, sku and warehouse must add up to minus the shipped quantity.
- Where nothing was recorded for a line, record it. Where a line was recorded with the wrong quantity, record one more adjustment with the difference, so the total comes out right. Where it was recorded correctly, record nothing.
- The export repeats one order. An order that appears twice shipped once.
- Some lines cannot be recorded because the warehouse does not have the stock. Do not record those lines at all, and write them to `/app/blocked.csv`, a CSV file with the header `order,sku,missing` and one row per such line, where `missing` is the quantity that still needed to be recorded.

Do not change any other stock.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

steps.reasoning_content: I need to pull up the existing adjustments, so I'll list them with pagination at five per page. Filtering by order reference could work, but manual records might carry a wrong reference or warehouse, so I'll skip the filter and fetch everything.

The 264 adjustments are too many pages to go through one by one, so I'll filter by reference for each of the 28 orders instead. The reference match should be exact, though the hand records might contain other things, so I'll check that as I go. I'll make the per-order calls in parallel, five pages each.

I'm sorting out which records are the hand-made ones: ids 240 through 264 make 25, and I've matched 23 of them so far. The two still missing, 260 and 261, are the ones tied to order 91042 on the first page, which accounts for the full count of 25.

Now I'm working out the stock adjustments for each order: first the quantities that don't match what's on hand, then the blocked items that need restocking before the remaining orders can be filled.

I'm checking whether the remaining orders have any records by reference, since the earlier non-hand records could still point to them. I'll do that check and pull stock levels for the blocked items together.

steps.reasoning_content:
I'm working out how to get the stock levels: pulling inventory per warehouse would mean many paged queries, so fetching individual items for the roughly 40 needed SKUs looks more practical. I'm also weighing just attempting the adjustments and letting them fail if stock is short, though the missing quantity still needs handling.

I'm weighing whether to check stock first, since competing orders on the same SKU and warehouse could clash and positive adjustments should go in before the decrements. Rather than querying every warehouse page by page, I'll fetch the roughly 35 unique SKUs involved in parallel.

Each warehouse only has 27 items, so paging through them would take 18 calls. I'm considering calling get_item directly instead, which would mean 17 calls across north pages 2-6, west pages 1-6, and east pages 1-6.

I'm working out that the rows missing from the list probably mean zero stock, since those items aren't in the warehouse. The north warehouse has 27 items, and I still need to check west pages 7 to 10 and east pages 7 to 11, along with whether specific SKUs like 1003 are stocked there.

I still need to pull the remaining west and east pages before I can confirm which items are actually missing.

I'm comparing the required quantities against the northern stock levels. Most items there have enough on hand, but item 1003 isn't stocked in the north, and since its 91190 line needs 3, that's a shortfall of 3.

I'm checking the northern needs item by item, and most are covered, but item 1059 needs 5 and only has 1, so that's blocked. Moving on to the western stock, everything there checks out with no shortfalls.

I'm checking the eastern stock now: most items are covered, but item 1004 needs 5 and only has 2, so that one's blocked. I'm also verifying the remaining eastern needs against their stock levels.

I've already worked through the northern, western, and eastern stock checks and found three blocked items. Now I'm confirming the remaining northern and eastern lines are covered, and then I'll make the adjustments in a parallel batch.

steps.reasoning_content: I'm looking into order 1020 west SO-91161, where record 273 was skipped, though it may have been recorded anyway, so I need to check.

I already applied that change, so I won't retry it. Next I'm going through the full set of new orders, leaving out the blocked lines: several west and north lines with their item counts, and one east line whose count is missing.

I'm listing the remaining order lines by warehouse, leaving out the three blocked ones, which comes to 41 calls. To keep errors from creating duplicates, I'll run them in batches and check each batch.

Item 91190 at HX-1003 north is blocked, and 1003 isn't in the north listing of 27 items. I'm inclined to trust the listing, though a quick get_item on 1003 would be cheap, so I'll do that single check.

arguments.command:
cd /app; printf 'order,sku,missing
SO-91190,HX-1003,3
SO-91049,HX-1059,5
SO-91197,HX-1004,5
' > blocked.csv
echo '{"status":"success","summary":"Corrected hand-recorded shipments and recorded all missing lines for 2026-09-13 (duplicate SO-91161 counted once). Three lines lacked stock (SO-91190, SO-91049, SO-91197) and were written to blocked.csv without being recorded."}' > STATUS.json

steps.message:
The stock records now match the 2026-09-13 export, except for three lines the warehouses couldn't cover. I made 52 adjustments (adj-265 to adj-316). I didn't re-query stock afterwards.

- **Corrections:**
  - Eleven hand-recorded lines had the wrong quantity, so I added a difference adjustment (some positive, some negative).
  - Where staff recorded a line correctly, I recorded nothing.
  - SO-91161 appears twice in the export and was handled once.
- **New records:** Lines with no record at all were recorded in full.
- **Blocked lines:** These were not recorded. They are in `/app/blocked.csv`:

| order | sku | missing |
|---|---|---|
| SO-91190 | HX-1003 | 3 |
| SO-91049 | HX-1059 | 5 |
| SO-91197 | HX-1004 | 5 |

  - HX-1003 isn't stocked in the north warehouse.
  - HX-1059 has only 1 on hand in north.
  - HX-1004 has only 2 on hand in east.
- **Method:** I checked existing records only by order reference, not by scanning all 264 adjustments. The 25 hand entries (adj-240 to adj-264) all carry order references, so I'm fairly confident none were missed.
- **Retry:** One call (SO-91161, HX-1020) returned a connection error. I checked, and the adjustment had gone through, so I didn't repeat it.

`/app/STATUS.json` is written with status `success`.
